name: Biore UV Aqua Rich

lead:
Biore UV Aqua Rich Watery Essence is a face-and-body sunscreen from Kao Corporation rated SPF50+ and PA++++. Its watery, non-sticky texture and lack of white cast make it a popular daily sunscreen in Japan and parts of Asia, and daily UV protection is what people use to limit sun-driven spots, freckles and uneven tone [1].
The listing describes it as usable as a makeup base, water resistant in an 80-minute test, and removable with soap. Published clinical studies on this specific product were not found [1].

paras: It is applied as the last skincare step in the morning and can go under foundation. Reviewers cite its hydrating, quick-absorbing feel, including when reapplied through the day [1].

Formulations differ by edition and country, with some versions listing different UV filters. A single editorial review reported lower real-world protection than the label, a claim whose method could not be verified. As with any sunscreen, individuals sensitive to ingredients may react.

chain: Fewer sun-induced spots and more even skin over time
angle.text: The product is worn daily to protect from UV, which the brand says helps prevent sunburn-related spots and freckles. Its light finish also lets it sit under makeup [1].

lead: Biore UV Aqua Rich Watery Essence is a sunscreen essence made by Kao Corporation, sold in drugstores and supermarkets in Japan and in some ASEAN markets, China and Taiwan [1].

It is rated SPF50+ and PA++++, comes in a 70 ml tube, and sold for about 968 yen in the listing consulted [1]. The brand highlights an even-application design, hyaluronic acid, royal jelly extract and butylene glycol as moisturizers [1].
People use it to prevent sun-related spots and freckles while keeping skin looking smooth under makeup [1].
infobox: Hyaluronic acid, royal jelly extract, BG

paras: The listing describes a watery, translucent essence that spreads easily, does not feel sticky and can be reapplied or layered; it is marketed as usable on face and body and as a makeup base [1].
Ingredient lists differ by regional edition: some versions list Tinosorb S and ethylhexyl triazone, others different filters, and a related mild variant states it omits avobenzone and oxybenzone [1].

User reviews highlight a hydrating feel and a lack of heaviness in hot weather [1]. One editorial review argues that UV camera and spectrophotometer tests suggest real-world protection may be lower than the labelled rating; its methodology was not verified.
